definitions.explanation: Whether the parts of a story, argument, or explanation fit together logically. Almost always used in the set phrase {辻褄|つじつま}が{合|あ}う (to be consistent) or {辻褄|つじつま}を{合|あ}わせる (to make things consistent).

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}は{辻褄|つじつま}が{合|あ}わない。
{無理|むり}に{辻褄|つじつま}を{合|あ}わせようとしても、すぐにばれる。
examples.english: Even if you try to force the story to be consistent, people will see through it right away.

examples.japanese: {証言|しょうげん}の{辻褄|つじつま}が{合|あ}っているかどうか、もう{一度|いちど}{確認|かくにん}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to check once more whether the testimony is consistent.

notes:
Rarely used alone — almost always appears in set phrases. The word comes from sewing terminology: {辻|つじ} (crossroads/seam intersection) + {褄|つま} (hem), referring to whether seams line up properly at their meeting points.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {辻褄|つじつま}が{合|あ}う (to be consistent, to add up)
- {辻褄|つじつま}が{合|あ}わない (to be inconsistent, not add up)
- {辻褄|つじつま}を{合|あ}わせる (to make things consistent, to reconcile)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {話|はなし}の{辻褄|つじつま} (consistency of a story)
- {辻褄|つじつま}の{合|あ}わない{説明|せつめい} (an inconsistent explanation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {整合性|せいごうせい}: consistency, coherence (formal, technical)
- {筋|すじ}が{通|とお}る: to make sense, to be logical (focuses on overall logic rather than specific matching)

cross_references.label: to make sense, to be logical
